items.prompt:
Engineers should
A) build the first idea only
B) compare several possible solutions
C) never test
D) avoid criteria

steps: Comparing several ideas leads to a better choice.

items.prompt:
Possible solutions are compared against the
A) criteria and constraints
B) weather
C) team's mood
D) color of the room

steps: Solutions are judged by the problem's goals and limits.

items.prompt:
A tool that helps compare solutions side by side is a
A) comparison table
B) hammer
C) stopwatch only
D) paintbrush

steps: A table lists each solution against each requirement.

items.prompt:
A design meets all the criteria but costs too much. It
A) is the best solution
B) breaks a constraint, so it is not ideal
C) has no problems
D) meets every constraint
items.answer: B) breaks a constraint, so it is not ideal

steps: Going over budget breaks the cost constraint.

items.prompt:
If two designs both stay within the constraints, choose the one that
A) looks coolest
B) meets the criteria better
C) is newest
D) was built first

steps: When both fit the limits, better criteria performance wins.

items.prompt:
Why generate more than one possible solution?
A) To waste time
B) To have options to compare and pick the best
C) To confuse the team
D) To avoid the criteria
items.answer: B) To have options to compare and pick the best

steps: More options improve the chance of a strong choice.

items.prompt:
Shade X blocks more sun but uses banned materials; Shade Y blocks a little less using allowed materials. The better choice is
A) Shade X, because it blocks more sun
B) Shade Y, because it stays within the material constraint
C) neither
D) both equally
items.answer: B) Shade Y, because it stays within the material constraint

steps: X breaks a constraint, so Y better fits the problem.

items.prompt:
The BEST solution is the one that
A) is cheapest no matter what
B) meets the criteria most completely while staying within the constraints
C) looks the nicest
D) was the first idea
items.answer: B) meets the criteria most completely while staying within the constraints

steps: The best solution balances meeting the criteria with staying in the limits.
